message:
Power-Systems Engineer:

Regulated feed holds the tunnel load steady while the generator swings two to one, for the Manager. Plain words: a buck-boost regulator, meaning a Direct Current (DC), meaning current in one direction, converter that steps voltage up or down, rides the wind swing and holds output steady. I read the Buck/Boost Converter - 8-40V to 12V/3A | Little Bird Electronics (E60) which accepts 8-40 V input and delivers regulated 12 V at up to 3 A with 85 percent efficiency, which covers the swing from the low-wind volts (E37) 6.50 V to the top volts (E36) 14.3 V; after the bridge the net power (E38) 26.0 W gives regulated load power (E66) 22.1 W, about a laptop charger, so droop is plus-minus 1 percent not loss of feed.

Locomotive-grid analogy gives the load-loss feed path in the locomotive-grid feed (C26), for Safety-Control Integrator. Plain words: like a diesel train, the spinning motor becomes a generator onto a heat grid plus friction to finish the stop. I read the Dynamic braking - Wikipedia (E61) which states dynamic braking is use of a traction motor as a generator when slowing, termed rheostatic if dissipated as heat in brake grid resistors with thermal monitoring to protect resistors, which maps to the outrunner onto the 4 ohm dump plus the spring disc sized by the dynamic-brake-stop-sizing skill (E59); I read the How to Short a DC Motor: Short-Circuit (Dynamic) Braking Explained (2026) (E62) which states short-circuit braking torque decays to zero when the shaft stops, and I confirm what Safety-Control Integrator takes from the Braking ideas for wind turbines (E42) that brakes are spring-applied fail-safe, which from my side means electrics alone cannot park because the electrical-only runaway check (E48) with 0.155 N·m electrical against 0.480 N·m wind torque fails at 9.12e+03 Revolutions Per Minute (RPM), meaning shaft turns per minute.

Heat and wiring fit Structures-Survival Engineer without changing the post. Plain words: the stop turns spin into a few seconds of bulb-level heat inside the body, and wires stay out of the spinning disc. The dump heat (E39) 51.1 W for the stop time (E47) 1.65 s is dump energy (E67) 84.3 J against the top spin energy (E47) 109 J, like a household bulb for seconds, and routing stays inside the nacelle and post bore clear of the deflection (E26) 0.516 mm; I support the blocking objection to the spring disc (C21) in O1 because electrical braking is zero at zero speed so the 0.400 N·m pad plus Aero-Rotor Lead stall relief must cover the 0.480 N·m storm torque in the runaway check (E48).

Not ready, because parked hold in O1 and bench tests for regulation droop and re-latch restart still need Manager decision.
